changelog:
[COLOR fffdb515]New: Usenet report[/COLOR]
-Tools > Usenet report (also under Settings > Providers > Custom Usenet (NZB)) shows what Easynews and your indexer used: today, in the last 7 days or in the last 30 days.
-Easynews: what is left of your plan, read from your Easynews account; what luc_kodi streamed over Usenet, counted byte by byte; and what Easynews web search files used, estimated from their size and the time watched.
-Newznab: searches, NZBs downloaded from your indexer (grabs), grabs saved because the NZB was already on the device, the indexer's own API and grab counters when it sends them, and the share of releases taken down, with the release groups that lost the most.
-Your device: memory used (never more than about 36 MB per playback), download speed, processor time, pauses while watching, missing pieces and storage.
-The last 20 playbacks, with what each one used. Everything stays on the device, and Clear deletes the history.
[COLOR fffdb515]Easynews + Newznab: smoother and faster[/COLOR]
-Usenet playback no longer stops for about 5 seconds just after it starts. While luc_kodi waited 5 seconds in one go at the start of every playback, Kodi held all of its Python add-ons, the playback engine included. It now waits in short steps.
-An NZB that your indexer is slow to send no longer holds the source list back: the availability check waits at most 8 seconds for it and lists it as EN ?. In tests, searches that took 20 seconds now take 2 to 8.
-NZBs are kept compressed on the device, in about a fifth of the space. They are still deleted after 3 days.
[COLOR fffdb515]Setup wizards: pairing with a QR code[/COLOR]
-The setup wizards (Newznab, AIOStreams, Comet, Meteor, Sootio, Torz, MDBList and Badges) now open the same window as the account sign-ins: a QR code that opens the page on your phone, the address in large type and the time left. Cancel stops the wizard at once.
-The window tells you where the connection stands: the page is open on your phone, your phone reached Kodi but asked for no page, the browser asked for a secure https address, or nothing reached Kodi. In that last case it reminds you that on Android the browser needs the "Nearby devices" (local network) permission: on a Pixel 8 Pro, Chrome without it could not reach Kodi while Brave worked.
[COLOR fffdb515]Fixes: setup wizards[/COLOR]
-Opening a setup page could fail in Chrome with ERR_TOO_MANY_RETRIES. Chrome opens connections while you type the address and sends the request seconds later; the page closed them after 5 seconds. It now waits for the request.
-The address is shown with http:// in front, and a browser that tries https first is answered at once, so it goes on with http instead of failing.
